analysis: The PR changes only docs/developer/test.md, which is developer documentation for tests and CI. It has no runtime code, no change to the provider/coordinator wire contract, and no key or attestation handling. I reviewed the full patch and the base text. The changes describe: (1) a CI restructuring where test jobs download build products and refuse products from another commit or toolchain version (a mild integrity improvement); (2) the audit warning for unweighted serial suites; (3) shard and job counts for the cluster runners; (4) retry rules for public prompt-fixture downloads. For the downloads, only transient transfer failures retry (at most 3 attempts). The docs state that SHA-256 mismatch, oversize body, Content-Length mismatch, cross-origin response and other non-200 statuses fail immediately, so integrity checks are retained. The MiMo scripts follow redirects to a different HTTPS host, but the downloads are hash-pinned and refuse plain HTTP, so this is not a regression. Documented caveats: the MiMo prompt script has no total deadline, only a 60 s socket timeout, which is a CI availability matter and not in the threat model; (5) job-size routing notes, which state that CI's request is byte-for-byte unchanged unless DARKBLOOM_JOB_SHAPES is exactly on. None of this touches T-041 (the prefix cache) or the TB-011/TB-012 boundaries, and the text mentioning SSD cache test fixtures is unchanged context. Residual uncertainty: the doc claims about scripts, workflows and artifact checks (the commit/toolchain refusal and the retry classification) are not verifiable from the supplied evidence, because the implementing scripts and workflow files are not in this batch. These are documentation claims and not security regressions. The patch excerpt was truncated, but the range map is complete and the base text matches.
